Choose which test data gsm.core uses

Source: R/testdata.R
use_testdata_snapshot.Rd

Usage

use_testdata_snapshot(dir = Sys.getenv("GSM_TESTDATA_SNAPSHOT"))

use_testdata_tag(tag = Sys.getenv("GSM_TESTDATA_TAG"))

Arguments

dir

character(1) Path to a local snapshot folder. NULL or "" stops using one.

tag

character(1) A release tag. NULL or "" stops pinning one.

Value

character(1) The previous value (or NULL), invisibly, so it can be restored later.

Details

By default, gsm.core uses the gsm.datasim test data release built with the gsm packages you have installed (see the "Release selection" section of lSource). These functions override that choice:

  • use_testdata_snapshot(): read from a local snapshot folder containing snapshot.json and the files it lists, e.g. an unzipped data-<id>.zip release asset, for offline work or to test an unpublished bundle. Nothing is downloaded or cached. The folder is used even if installed packages are newer than the snapshot (with a message). Takes priority over use_testdata_tag().

  • use_testdata_tag(): use one exact gsm.datasim release, e.g. "data-8cde53949d4d".

Each function's default reads an environment variable (GSM_TESTDATA_SNAPSHOT, GSM_TESTDATA_TAG). gsm.core calls both with their defaults when it loads, so setting the variables (e.g. in .Renviron or CI) applies them every session. Calling a function changes the setting for the current session only.

A folder is checked as soon as it's set (or, for GSM_TESTDATA_SNAPSHOT, when gsm.core loads, with a warning instead of an error). A tag is checked when the test data is next accessed.

Examples

old <- use_testdata_tag("data-8cde53949d4d")
use_testdata_tag(old)

# Re-read the environment variable:
use_testdata_tag()

# Temporarily, e.g. in a test:
# withr::defer(use_testdata_tag(use_testdata_tag("data-...")))
